name: ui-design
description: End-to-end UI design for a page or app screen. Brainstorms the visual direction, gathers references from the user or a curated template library, composes a token system, builds it, inspects it in a real browser, roasts it with parallel critics, fixes what they find, and reports the cost.

phases.goal: Establish what the page is for, who it is for, and what a good version of it looks like - before any pixel is chosen.
phases.gate: The direction is written down and the user has confirmed it. A direction nobody can repeat back is not a direction.
phases.notes: design-is audits against Rams' principles and hands off to make-plan for one of new / refine / redesign. Use it when the brief is fuzzy about taste, not when it is clear.

phases.goal: Lock the visual language by combining what the user already loves with what the template library can offer.
inputs: user-supplied references (URLs, screenshots, brand assets, competitor pages)
phases.gate: Palette, type and layout archetype are chosen and locked.

two_paths.user_has_references: Read them. Extract the actual rules: what colours, what type, what density, what spacing rhythm. Write the rules down as tokens, not as vibes.
two_paths.user_has_no_references: Offer CHOICES, never a blank page. The library under design-taste-frontend/library/ holds researched directions (directions.json), palettes.json, type.json, sections.json, heroes.json, motions.json, motifs (tells.json). Pick 3-4 internally consistent combinations and present them with previews - palette swatches, type specimens, and the section blueprint - so the user picks with their eyes, not with adjectives.

phases.notes: Never present one option. Three to four, side by side, each internally consistent. If the user says 'whatever', pick the one that best fits the stated audience and say why.

phases.goal: Turn the chosen direction into a token system and layout rules that every later screen obeys.
outputs: colour tokens with roles, not raw hex
motion tokens with durations and easing
phases.gate: Tokens are written to a file that the build phase imports, not to a doc that describes them.
phases.notes: design-taste-frontend/library/app.css and base.css are a working token example - read them before inventing your own.

phases.goal: Implement the page so it honours the tokens.
phases.gate: The page renders. Then the next phase proves it looks right.
phases.notes: impeccable's own reference files (layout.md, colorize.md, animate.md, harden.md, craft.md) are the per-task references. Read the one you need, not the whole set.

phases.goal: Look at the actual rendered result with real eyes, in a real browser.
phases.gate: You have actually looked at a screenshot. Reasoning about how it probably looks is not inspection.
phases.how: design-taste-frontend/scripts/inspect.mjs renders and captures; lint.mjs enforces the house style. Both are the reason this skillset can catch slop that a code review cannot.
phases.notes: This phase is the single highest-value phase in the skillset. Skipping it is how pages ship looking generic.

phases.goal: Find what is actually wrong, from three different angles at once.
outputs: ranked findings: severity, location, the specific problem, the fix
phases.gate: Every finding is actionable. 'Looks generic' is not a finding; 'the hero headline uses the templated centred-hero pattern that appears in 90% of the corpus' is.
phases.how: Spawn 2-3 critics in parallel, each with one lens: visual taste, accessibility and correctness, and would-a-user-want-this. Use workflows/roast-and-fix.workflow.js to automate the loop.
phases.notes: impeccable/critique.md is the deepest single reference here (47.8K). Read it when the visual findings are hard to see.

phases.goal: Apply the findings that are worth fixing, then prove the fixes worked.
outputs: a list of findings deliberately not fixed, with reasons
phases.gate: Re-inspected after fixing. A fix that was not re-checked is not a fix.
phases.notes: Expect 2-3 iterations. One pass rarely clears a roast.

phases.goal: Report what the page cost to produce and what it will cost to load.
phases.gate: Reported. A cost number nobody saw cannot be improved.
phases.notes: If bundle size is over budget, the fix usually lives in phase 4, not phase 8. Say so.

must: The direction was chosen by the user, from options, with their eyes on previews - or, if the user waived it, chosen by you with a stated reason.
Tokens exist as a file the build imports.
The page was screenshotted at three breakpoints and the screenshots were actually looked at.
At least two critics reviewed it, and their findings were either fixed or explicitly declined with a reason.
The page was re-inspected after the last fix.
fails: Presenting a single reference option instead of choices.
Declining every finding because fixing is expensive.
